titulo: agente-ready: a 0–100 score with weights you can change
lead: "AI readiness" scanners give you a score, but almost none publish how it is calculated. agente-ready keeps each weight, the reason, and the source in a versioned file, pesos.json. You get your site's score, see what weighs most, and if you disagree with a weight, you change it and run again.
objetivo: get your site's readiness score and change one weight in pesos.json to see the score change.

aprende.t: The 6 categories and the weight of each criterion
How the score is calculated (and what leaves the denominator)
Why llms.txt weighs 2 and WebMCP is preparation

hero_alt: An inspector with a clipboard checks a list in front of the door of a commercial building.

secoes.sub: Weights add up to 100. Tap each step.

nos.detalhe: Reads the home page and a few pages spread across the sitemap (--paginas, default 4), the robots.txt, up to 8 same-origin scripts, and the llms.txt. That's 10 to 25 requests, with a 1 s pause. It's a thermometer; for the whole site, use the auditor.

Each criterion has a weight, a reason, and a source in pesos.json (v1.0.0, 10/19/2026). The informational ones (training blocked, Content-Signal, Markdown response) weigh 0: they show up, they don't count.
Each criterion comes out ok, partial, or fail. What doesn't apply (a site with no forms, no languages, no WebMCP for the policy check) leaves the denominator: it doesn't count as a fail.
Points earned divided by the sum of the weights that apply, times 100. The report shows the score by category and what weighs most, so you fix that first.

secoes.legenda: A score with the math in the open: you can disagree with a number and show why.

secoes.titulo: The criteria that weigh the most

texto: robots.txt lets search bots (12) and user-requested agents (6) in; the CDN does not block the User-Agent of OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, and Perplexity-User (12).
If a bot can't read the page, nothing else matters to it.
150+ words in the delivered HTML (10), a visible answer with a main heading and paragraph (6), authorship (5), and date (5).
Authorship and date are what event sites and landing pages lack most.
Organization or Person with @id in the home page JSON-LD (8), sameAs for the official profiles (4), and a link to About or Contact (2).
This is the "who publishes" that course 2 teaches you to build.
llms.txt weighs 2: in the Ahrefs study (137 thousand domains, 06/15/2026), 97% of the files received no requests at all.

WebMCP weighs 8 in total: a tool registered with document.modelContext.registerTool() is worth 5. The specification is a W3C community draft (10/16/2026); the old API name earns partial credit, with a warning.

exemplo.texto: WebMCP is preparation for agents, not a ranking factor. llms.txt is cheap and optional, not a citation lever.

secoes.titulo: Get the score and change a weight
secoes.sub: Run it from the ferramentas/agente-ready folder.

blocos.conteudo:
cd ferramentas/agente-ready
python3 agente-ready.py https://yoursite.com --saida nota/yoursite

cp pesos.json my-weights.json
# open my-weights.json and change the "peso" of one criterion (e.g.: webmcp_api from 5 to 0)
python3 agente-ready.py https://yoursite.com --pesos my-weights.json --saida nota/yoursite-my-weights

# Weights for <yoursite.com> — <dd/mm/yyyy>
criterion: <criterion id>
original weight: <n>  →  my weight: <n>
reason: <e.g.: my audience doesn't use browser agents; WebMCP is a draft with no stable browser>
score with pesos.json: <n>  ·  score with my weights: <n>

abas.html:
www.inema.club: nota 93/100 (5 páginas, 22 requisições).
  [falha, peso 2] Link para Sobre ou Contato na home: sem link /sobre, /about ou /contato

eventos.inema.pro: nota 69/100 (5 páginas, 15 requisições).
  [falha, peso 8] Organization ou Person com @id no JSON-LD da home: 0 entidade(s); com @id: 0
  [falha, peso 5] Autoria identificada: 0 de 5 com autor (meta, rel=author ou JSON-LD)
  [falha, peso 5] Data de publicação ou atualização: 0 de 5 com data (JSON-LD, meta article ou <time>)
  [falha, peso 5] Ferramentas WebMCP registradas com document.modelContext.registerTool(): nenhum registerTool() em 2 script(s) de mesma origem + inline

The same eventos.inema.pro with webmcp_api from 5 to 0 in my-weights.json:

eventos.inema.pro: nota 73/100 (5 páginas, 15 requisições).
  [falha, peso 8] Organization ou Person com @id no JSON-LD da home: 0 entidade(s); com @id: 0
  [falha, peso 5] Autoria identificada: 0 de 5 com autor (meta, rel=author ou JSON-LD)
  [falha, peso 5] Data de publicação ou atualização: 0 de 5 com data (JSON-LD, meta article ou <time>)
  [falha, peso 4] sameAs ligando a entidade aos perfis oficiais: sem sameAs na entidade

The math: 66 points earned out of 95 applicable gives 69; out of 90, it gives 73. The list of what to fix first did not change order at the top.

• Treating the score as a ranking: the weights are an editorial decision by INEMA, with a source for the why, not for the number.
  • Changing a weight to make the score go up: change it when you have a reason and write it down; the criterion stays in the report.
  • Expecting to see a WebMCP tool from another origin: detection is static; a script from another domain, loaded later or in an iframe does not show up.

secoes.titulo: Practice: the score and your weight
secoes.sub: In lesson 7 the score joins the monthly routine.

exercicios.texto: Run agente-ready on your site and write down the score and the 3 failing criteria with the highest weight.
exercicios.pronto: you have the score, the 3 criteria with the weight of each, and the evidence the report shows.

exercicios.texto: Copy pesos.json, change one weight with a written reason, and run again with --pesos.
exercicios.pronto: the "why I changed the weight" template is filled in with both scores, and they are different.

secoes.sub: The explanation shows up after your answer.

perguntas.p: Your site has no form. What happens to the 4 points for forms?
opcoes: They become a failure and the score drops.
They leave the denominator: they count neither for nor against.
The tool stops with an error.
perguntas.explica: A criterion that does not apply is left out of the math. The score is points earned divided by the applicable weights.

opcoes: Because it is hard to do.
Because in the largest public study, 97% of the files received no requests at all.
perguntas.explica: It is cheap and useful as an index for coding agents, but there is no evidence it leads to citation. Google's AI guide says it may ignore it.

perguntas.p: In the eventos.inema.pro output, what matters most for raising the score?
opcoes: Entity with @id on the home page (8), and authorship and date on the pages (5 + 5).
perguntas.explica: The output lists the failures by weight. llms.txt was already fine. Blocking training is informational and does not change the score.

perguntas.p: Does WebMCP registered on the site guarantee a citation in ChatGPT?
opcoes: No: it's a community draft, with no stable browser support; it counts as preparation.
Yes, if the weight is high.
perguntas.explica: The specification itself says it is not a W3C standard. It prepares the site for agents in the browser; it is not a ranking factor.

itens.texto: Weights, reason and source in pesos.json; whatever doesn't apply is left out of the denominator.
Bot access (30) and extractable content (26) come before everything else.
llms.txt is optional (weight 2); WebMCP is preparation, not ranking.
